name: P21

lead: P21 is a small peptide derived from CNTF, a neurotrophic protein. It is discussed as a nootropic aimed at memory and focus.
Animal studies reported increased neurogenesis and better memory in aged and Alzheimer-model mice. People in nootropic communities use it for cognition and long-term brain support.

paras: The compound is described in the research literature as a neurogenic and neurotrophic peptide that raises BDNF-related signaling and supports synapses and new neurons in the dentate gyrus.
No approved human use exists, and published work is in animals and cells. It is a research compound, and gray-market products are not regulated as medicines.

angle.text: Users take P21 as a nootropic peptide for memory and focus, which supports study, work and training routines. Its link to appearance is through that general performance theme.

lead: P21 (also written P021) is a short synthetic peptide designed from a region of ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF), a protein that supports nerve cells. It is sold and discussed as a nootropic peptide, with users interested in memory and focus; its relevance to looks is indirect, through the cognitive and recovery goals people attach to it.[1]

Published work on the compound is in animal models, where studies from a group including Iqbal and colleagues report that P021 promoted neurogenesis in the dentate gyrus and reduced memory decline in aging, Alzheimer-model and Down syndrome-model mice.[1] Note that "p21" is also the name of an unrelated cell-cycle protein (CDKN1A), which dominates search results.
infobox: Mice (Alzheimer, aging, Down syndrome, CDKL5 models)

paras: No studies found. Animal research reports that P021 prevented dendritic and synaptic deficits and cognitive impairment, reduced cognitive aging, and rescued memory deficits in Alzheimer and Down syndrome mouse models.[1]
The p21 protein (CDKN1A, WAF1/CIP1) is a cell-cycle inhibitor involved in cancer biology and is a separate topic.[2]
